text: I think it's a misconception. I have never had anything against delivery business, per se. I think... They are non-competing businesses with each other. And I deeply appreciate the role aggregators have played in growing that segment of the business. What I am against is the tyranny of the aggregators, not the aggregators themselves. And I want there to be a level playing field. I want our agreements to be not unilateral. I want there to be fair play and fairness in the way it is conducted. And I think that we echo the same pain points of the entire industry. So we're not against delivery at all, because we don't think that dining out is competing with eating at home. They are two separate businesses. dining out will always remain dining out. And I think COVID really brought home this point because while all the pundits and all these tech pundits were predicting that, oh, you know, nobody's ever going to go and shop offline again and everything's going to happen online. Nobody's ever going to go to the restaurant again and everybody's going to, you know, order in. All that has just proven to be complete. It's been completely debunked. I think that you can never ever, in fact, what COVID has taught us is that you can never ever replace dining. And because dining out is not consuming food, right? Dining out is, it's not even an experience. It is a get together with your friends. It's a gossip session. It is a celebration of a little victory. It is celebrating a birthday. A anniversary is going somewhere to forget about your breakup. is going there to meet people. It is human behavior and that's never going to change. What delivery business is competing is that, okay, I've made food at home, it's very boring, so I'll eat outside. So delivery business is competing with your kitchen. It's not competing with the experience of dining out. So that's a misnomer. And I have nothing against delivery portals. They are all friends of mine. I think the NRAI is what stands in between complete annihilation of the industry and the tyranny of aggregators. And that needs to be kept in check.
